title: OpenAI released a new cybersecurity model. Is that enough?
slides: OpenAI shipped a cybersecurity model — does it actually protect anyone?
Built to find software vulnerabilities before attackers do
But it missed flaws human researchers caught instantly
Your security team can't simply trust automated scanners yet
Test it on one known vulnerability before trusting it
thread_text:
1. Security AI That Misses Flaws

OpenAI's new model aims to find software vulnerabilities before attackers do, but in early tests it overlooked bugs that human researchers caught instantly.

2. Built to Outpace Attackers

Automated scanning promises speed, but the gap between AI detection and human intuition is still wide open.

3. The Blind Spot Problem

One missed flaw can be a backdoor. Relying solely on automated scanners could leave your systems exposed to threats they never see.

4. Trust Isn't Automatic

Your security team can't simply trust automated scanners yet—especially when a single oversight can compromise everything.

5. Test Before You Trust

Take one known vulnerability and run it through the model. If it misses, you know the limits. Start there.

instagram.caption:
Its scanner missed bugs human researchers caught instantly. 👀

OpenAI shipped a cybersecurity model built to find software vulnerabilities before attackers do.

But early tests show it overlooked flaws a person spotted right away.

One missed flaw can act like a backdoor.

So your security team can't just trust automated scanners yet. 🔍

If you build or publish software, test the model on one known vulnerability first.

If it misses, you've found its limits before an attacker does. ⚠️

Would you trust it on your codebase today? 🤔
